newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hanbo H1 recurring loss at 84.1 bln won.
newsitem.headline: Hanbo H1 recurring loss at 84.1 bln won.

text.p: South Korea's failed Hanbo Steel Co posted 84.1 billion won in recurring loss in the first half of calendar 1997 against a 91.8 billion won loss a year earlier, a spokesman for the company's management said on Monday.
The nation's second-largest steelmaker has been run by court-appointed management since March after it was declared insolvent in January.
A senior official at the public information team for the management said Hanbo recorded 299.2 billion won in sales during the January-June period, against 332.6 billion won a year ago.

He said the company posted a loss even though a court had exempted all responsibilities by Hanbo to redeem its liabilites, which could help reduce financing costs in the company. Rising sales costs were cited as a reason contributing to the loss.
After a failed auction due to no bids, creditors rescheduled to sell the steelmaker on July 29.
An accounting company earlier estimated Hanbo's liabilities at 6.61 trillion won, compared to assets of 4.97 trillion.
